---
title: "Class 6. Split, apply, combine (solutions)"
format: html
---

Teacher version. Chunks run, so the data must exist: run sections 1 and 2 first.

```{r}
#| label: setup
pacman::p_load(here, tidyverse, janitor, countrycode)
```

## 1. Download the CSV once

```{r}
#| label: download
#| eval: false
read_csv("https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/e/2PACX-1vQMKvrshkL1R55vcnXnXQ14VfJM6HB62bed8U6ukVc-9ncRg79co2GoaS84eb1o4aEg1bqLFiWNJAS3/pub?gid=554197504&single=true&output=csv") |>
  write_csv(here("data", "gapminder.csv"))
```

## 2. Add continent and subregion

```{r}
#| label: prepare
here("data", "gapminder.csv") |>
  read_csv(show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  clean_names() |>
  rename(population = pop, income = gdp_percap) |>
  mutate(
    continent = countrycode(country, origin = "country.name", destination = "continent"),
    subregion = countrycode(country, origin = "country.name", destination = "un.regionsub.name"),
    .after = country
  ) |>
  write_csv(here("data", "gapminder_regions.csv"))
```

## 3. Check

```{r}
#| label: check
here("data", "gapminder_regions.csv") |>
  read_csv(show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(is.na(continent)) |>
  distinct(country)
```

If a name appears, `countrycode` did not recognise it. Fix it with `custom_match = c("Name in the file" = "Europe")` inside `countrycode()`.

## 4. A third column

```{r}
#| label: wb-region
here("data", "gapminder.csv") |>
  read_csv(show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  clean_names() |>
  mutate(
    wb_region = countrycode(country, origin = "country.name", destination = "region")
  ) |>
  distinct(wb_region)
```

## 5. Count

```{r}
#| label: count-subregion
here("data", "gapminder_regions.csv") |>
  read_csv(show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(year == 2007) |>
  count(subregion) |>
  arrange(desc(n))
```

## 6. Mean of countries and mean of people

```{r}
#| label: weighted
here("data", "gapminder_regions.csv") |>
  read_csv(show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(year == 2007) |>
  group_by(continent) |>
  summarize(
    mean_life = mean(life_exp),
    weighted_life = weighted.mean(life_exp, population)
  )
```

Large countries (China, India) pull the weighted mean of Asia away from the mean of countries. Ask which number answers "how long does a person in Asia live?".

## 7. Life expectancy by continent over time

```{r}
#| label: line
here("data", "gapminder_regions.csv") |>
  read_csv(show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  group_by(continent, year) |>
  summarize(life_exp = weighted.mean(life_exp, population), .groups = "drop") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = life_exp, color = continent)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1)
```

## 8. Median income, 1952 and 2007

```{r}
#| label: income
here("data", "gapminder_regions.csv") |>
  read_csv(show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(year %in% c(1952, 2007)) |>
  group_by(continent, year) |>
  summarize(median_income = median(income), .groups = "drop") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = continent, y = median_income, fill = factor(year))) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge")
```

## 9. The subregions of Europe

```{r}
#| label: europe
here("data", "gapminder_regions.csv") |>
  read_csv(show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  filter(continent == "Europe") |>
  group_by(subregion, year) |>
  summarize(life_exp = weighted.mean(life_exp, population), .groups = "drop") |>
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = life_exp, color = subregion)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1)
```
